metadata.title: Another proof of M. Kontsevich formality theorem for $\mathbb{R}^n$
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: metadata.json has empty authors/year; PDF first page lists Dmitry E. Tamarkin and dates the v4 arXiv submission 24 Sep 1998. Title in PDF matches registry (modulo $\mathbb{R}^n$).

nodes.name: Operad shift $O\{m\}$
nodes.statement: For a dg-operad $O$, define $O\{m\} = O \otimes \mathrm{Comm}\{m\}$ where $\mathrm{Comm}\{m\}(n) = \Lambda_n^{\otimes m}[(n-1)m]$, so that an $O\{m\}$-algebra on $V$ is the same as an $O$-algebra on $V[m]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Operadic shift functor that shifts the underlying complex of an algebra by $m$.

nodes.name: Koszul dual cooperad $O^\vee$ and homotopy $O$-algebras
nodes.statement: For a Koszul operad $O$, the Koszul dual cooperad $O^\vee$ is cogenerated by $O^\vee(2) \cong O(2)[1]$. A homotopy $O$-algebra on $V$ is a differential on the cofree $O^\vee$-coalgebra $S_{O^\vee} V$.
nodes.statement_clean: Recalls Koszul-dual cooperad and the cofree-coalgebra description of homotopy algebras.

nodes.name: Operad $HE_2$ (homotopy Gerstenhaber operad) via $P(V[1])$
nodes.statement: Let $P(V) \cong S_{e_2\{-1\}^*} V$ be the cofree $e_2\{-1\}^*$-coalgebra. Then $Q(V) \cong P(V[1])[-1]$ and a homotopy $e_2$-algebra on $V$ is a differential on $P(V[1])$, which carries comultiplication and cobracket of degrees $+1$ and $0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Concrete description of the operad $HE_2$ governing homotopy Gerstenhaber algebras as differentials on $P(V[1])$.

nodes.name: Operad $B_\infty$
nodes.statement: $B_\infty = B\{1\}$, where $B$-algebra structure on $V$ is equivalent to a dg-bialgebra structure on $TV$ with standard coproduct, unit, counit and a differential $D$ whose restriction to $V \cong T^1 V$ is the differential on $V$. Generated by maps $m_k: T^k V \to V$ and $m_{k,l}: T^k V \otimes T^l V \to V$.
nodes.statement_clean: Operad governing $B_\infty$-algebras (Hochschild-cochain-like algebras).

nodes.name: $X$-algebra with unit on a coalgebra $W$
nodes.statement: For an asymmetric operad $X$ in dg-coalgebras with counit and a marked element $e$ of a dg-coalgebra $W$, an $X$-algebra with unit $e$ on $W$ is a collection of coalgebra morphisms $\phi_n: X(n) \otimes W^{\otimes n} \to W$ that represent $X$ as a dg-operad and satisfy $\phi_0(1,1) = e$, $\phi_1(1,x) = x$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines algebras over an operad in coalgebras, with a marked unit element.

nodes.name: $XB$-algebra on $V$
nodes.statement: An $XB$-algebra on a complex $V$ is an $X$-algebra with unit on $TV$ (the tensor coalgebra), where $TV$ carries the standard coproduct, unit, counit, and a (not uniquely determined) differential as in section 2.1.5.
nodes.statement_clean: Specialization of $X$-algebras to the tensor coalgebra $TV$, recovering bialgebra-style structures.

nodes.name: Functor $O(\cdot)$ on operads of coalgebras
nodes.statement: $O(X)$ is the operad of $(n,1)$-ary operations of the PROP $P(X)$ governing $XB$-algebras; it is a functor from the category $C$ of operads of dg-coalgebras with counit acting trivially on $0$- and $1$-ary parts to dg-operads.
nodes.statement_clean: Functor producing a dg-operad from an operad in coalgebras, used to build both $B_\infty$ and $F$.

nodes.name: Asymmetric operad $As$ with $0$-ary operations
nodes.statement: Enrich the asymmetric operad $As$ governing associative algebras by setting $As(0) = k$ with structure maps $\circ_r^{p,q}(1 \otimes 1) = 1$ and giving each $As(k)$ the coalgebra structure $\Delta 1 = 1 \otimes 1$. Then $B = O(As)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Enriched operad of associative algebras (with nullary operation), realising $B$ as $O(As)$.

nodes.name: Operad $A$ from Stasheff associahedra
nodes.statement: $A$ is the operad of dg-coalgebras with counit defined by $A(n)_i = C_{-i}(K(n))$, where $K$ is the Stasheff topological asymmetric operad of associahedra equipped with a polyhedral decomposition and $0$-ary operations as in 6.3. Used to define $F = O(A)\{1\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Operad built from chains on Stasheff associahedra; serves as input to the functor $O(\cdot)$ to produce $F$.

nodes.name: Cone $\mathrm{Con}\, A$ of a dg-coalgebra
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Con}\, A$ is the colimit of $A \to k \leftarrow \mathrm{Cyl}\, A$, with $\mathrm{Cyl}\, A = C_\bullet(I) \otimes A$. As a vector space $\mathrm{Con}\, A \cong A \oplus A[-1] \oplus k$, with explicit comultiplication $\Delta_{\mathrm{Con}\, A}(Tu) = (T \otimes \mathrm{Id})\Delta u + e \otimes Tu$ and differential $d(Tu) = u - Tdu - \varepsilon(u)e$.
nodes.statement_clean: Cone construction in the category of dg-coalgebras, used inductively to extend the coalgebra structure across $K(n)$.

nodes.name: Operad $F$ and its sibling $G$
nodes.statement: $F = O(A)\{1\}$ and $G = O(A)$. The map $\varepsilon: A \to As$ produces $t': G \to B$ and $t: F \to B_\infty$, and via $k$ a map $r: F \to B_\infty \to e_2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Definition of the central operad $F$ used throughout the proof, plus its unshifted version $G$.

nodes.name: Filtration $F^k$ on $P(A)$ and $G$
nodes.statement: $F^0 P(A)(n,m) = P(A)(n,m)$; $F^1 P(A)(n,m) = 0$ if $n \geq m$ and equals $P(A)(n,m)$ if $n > m$; $F^k P(A)(n,m)$ is the span of compositions of $\geq k$ operations of which at least $k$ lie in $F^1 P(A)$. The induced filtration on $G$ counts internal vertices of trees.
nodes.statement_clean: Filtration on $P(A)$ inducing the filtration of $G$ by number of internal tree vertices.

nodes.name: Fundamental classes $\mu_k$
nodes.statement: $\mu_k \in C_{k-2}(K(k))$ is the fundamental class; $\mu_k \in V(k)$ and satisfies $d\mu_k = \sum_{i=2}^{k-1} \mu_i\{\mu_{k+1-i}\}$ where $\mu_i\{\mu_j\} = \sum_{k=1}^{i} (-1)^{(k-1)(j-1)} \circ_k^{i,j}(\mu_i, \mu_j)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Fundamental chains of associahedra; their boundary relations supply the $A_\infty$-like identities used later.

nodes.name: Main theorem (Theorem 2.1)
nodes.statement: There exists a morphism of operads $q: HE_2 \to B_\infty$ such that (1) $q \circ \phi = (\text{Lie}\{1\} \to B_\infty)$ via the canonical maps, and (2) the induced map $q^*: H^\bullet(HE_2) \to H^\bullet(B_\infty(2))$ together with the iso $\kappa: H^\bullet(B_\infty(2)) \cong e_2(2)$ recovers the canonical iso $H^\bullet(HE_2) \cong e_2(2)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Existence of an operad morphism $HE_2 \to B_\infty$ compatible with the Lie part and inducing the canonical Gerstenhaber structure on cohomology.
conclusions: Existence of $q: HE_2 \to B_\infty$ making diagram (5) commute
$q$ induces the iso $H^\bullet(HE_2) \cong e_2(2)$ via $\kappa$ (diagram (6))

nodes.name: Auxiliary theorem (Theorem 4.1)
nodes.statement: There exist an operad $F$, a quasiisomorphism $qis: F \to e_2$, a map $r: F \to B_\infty$, and a map $s: \mathrm{Holie} \to F$ making diagrams (9) and (10) commute, with $H^\bullet(F(2)) \to e_2(2)$ matching $r^*$ on $H^\bullet(B_\infty(2))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Reformulates Theorem 2.1 in terms of an operad $F$ that quasi-isomorphically maps to $e_2$ and compatibly to $B_\infty$.
conclusions: Existence of $F$ and maps $r, qis, s$ with the stated commutativity

nodes.name: Main reduction (Theorem 4.2)
nodes.statement: (1) There exists $k: B_\infty \to e_2$ with $k_*$ on $H^\bullet(B_\infty(2))$ equal to (2). (2) There exist an operad $F$ and maps $s: \mathrm{Holie}\{1\} \to F$, $t: F \to B_\infty$ with diagram (11) commuting. (3) The composition $r = k \circ t$ is a quasiisomorphism.
nodes.statement_clean: Three-part theorem whose conjunction implies Theorem 4.1: existence of $k$, existence of $F$ with $s,t$, and quasi-isomorphism of $r$.
conclusions: Existence of $k: B_\infty \to e_2$ with prescribed $k_*$
Existence of operad $F$ with maps $s, t$ making (11) commute
$r = k \circ t: F \to e_2$ is a quasiisomorphism

nodes.name: Etingof-Kazhdan quantization theorem
nodes.statement: For a Lie bialgebra $a$ there exist $k[[h]]$-linear maps $m: U(a) \otimes U(a)[[h]] \to U(a)[[h]]$ and $\Delta: U(a)[[h]] \to U(a) \otimes U(a)[[h]]$ making $(U(a)[[h]], m, \Delta)$ a bialgebra, with $m, \Delta$ standard mod $O(h)$ and $\Delta a - \Delta^{op} a = h\delta a + O(h^2)$ on $a$.
nodes.statement_clean: Quantization of Lie bialgebras producing a bialgebra deformation of $U(a)[[h]]$.
assumptions: $a$ is a (dg) Lie bialgebra over $k$ of characteristic $0$
conclusions: Existence of $k[[h]]$-linear bialgebra structure on $U(a)[[h]]$ extending the standard one
Quasi-classical limit recovers the Lie bialgebra structure on $a$
nodes.origin_citation: Etingof-Kazhdan, Quantization of Lie Bialgebras, Selecta Math 2 (1996)

nodes.name: Kontsevich formality theorem
nodes.statement: For $A = S\mathbb{R}^n$ or $C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)$, the Hochschild cochain complex $C^\bullet(A,A)$ is formal as a Gerstenhaber algebra, i.e., quasi-isomorphic to its cohomology $HH^\bullet(A,A)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Cited theorem the paper offers an alternative proof of: formality of Hochschild cochains as a Gerstenhaber algebra.
conclusions: $C^\bullet(A,A)$ is formal as a Gerstenhaber algebra
nodes.origin_citation: M. Kontsevich, Deformation quantization of Poisson Manifolds, I

nodes.name: Cohomology of $B(2)$ and $B_\infty(2)$
nodes.statement: $H^\bullet(B(2))$ is generated by the class of $m_{1,1}(x_1,x_2)-m_{1,1}(x_2,x_1)$ in $H^0(B(2))$ and $\tfrac{1}{2}(m_2(x_1,x_2)-m_2(x_2,x_1))$ in $H^1(B(2))$. These yield the iso $\kappa: H^\bullet(B_\infty(2)) \cong e_2(2)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Identifies the cohomology generators of $B(2)$ and $B_\infty(2)$ and produces the canonical iso to $e_2(2)$.
conclusions: Explicit generators of $H^\bullet(B(2))$ and $H^\bullet(B_\infty(2))$
Isomorphism $\kappa: H^\bullet(B_\infty(2)) \cong e_2(2)$

nodes.name: Equivalence of $B_\infty$-coalgebras with topological bialgebras
nodes.statement: The category of $B_\infty$-coalgebras is equivalent to the category whose objects are topological dg-bialgebras isomorphic to $\Pi TV[1]$ as topological algebras with unit and having $\varepsilon$ as counit, with morphisms induced by linear maps $V \to W$.
nodes.statement_clean: Reformulates $B_\infty$-coalgebras as topological dg-bialgebra structures on $\Pi TV[1]$, used to construct $B_\infty \to e_2$.
conclusions: Equivalence of categories between $B_\infty$-coalgebras and topological dg-bialgebras of the stated form

nodes.name: Lemma 4.1: cofibration
nodes.statement: The map $\phi: \mathrm{Holie}\{1\} \to HE_2$ from (4) is a cofibration in the closed model category of dg $k$-operads.
nodes.statement_clean: The canonical resolution map is a cofibration, so it has the right lifting property used to extract $q$ from $r$ and $s$.
conclusions: $\phi: \mathrm{Holie}\{1\} \to HE_2$ is a cofibration

nodes.name: Lemma 6.3: triangularity of $XB$-operations
nodes.statement: For an $XB$-algebra: $\phi^r_{k_1\ldots k_n} = 0$ for $r > k_1 + \ldots + k_n$, and $D_k^l = 0$ for $l > k$ with $D_k^k$ the differential induced by $d$ on $V$.
nodes.statement_clean: Operations of an $XB$-algebra are upper-triangular with respect to tensor degree.
assumptions: $X$ an asymmetric operad of coalgebras as in 6.1.1
conclusions: $\phi^r_{k_1\ldots k_n}$ vanishes for $r > \sum k_i$
$D_k^l$ vanishes for $l > k$ and equals the induced differential when $l = k$

nodes.name: Proposition 6.4: presentation of $XB$-algebras
nodes.statement: An $XB$-algebra structure on $(V,d)$ is the same as a collection of maps $\phi^r_{k_1\ldots k_n}: X(n) \otimes T^{k_1} V \otimes \ldots \otimes T^{k_n} V \to T^r V$ ($r \leq \sum k_i$, degree $0$) and $D_l^m: T^l V \to T^m V$ ($l > m > 0$, degree $1$) satisfying explicit identities (13)-(16).
nodes.statement_clean: Concrete presentation of $XB$-algebra structures by structure maps and explicit relations.
assumptions: $X$ an asymmetric operad of coalgebras with counit
conclusions: Equivalence of $XB$-algebra structures with the listed maps and identities

nodes.name: Proposition 6.5: PROP $P(X)$ governs $XB$-algebras
nodes.statement: $XB$-algebras are governed by a dg PROP $P(X)$ generated by $\phi(x)^r_{k_1\ldots k_n}$ ($x \in X(n)$ homogeneous, degree $|x|$) and $D_l^m$ (degree $1$), with relations and differential as in Proposition 6.4.
nodes.statement_clean: Identifies the universal dg-PROP that governs $XB$-algebra structures.
assumptions: $X$ an asymmetric operad of coalgebras with counit
conclusions: $XB$-algebras correspond to representations of $P(X)$

nodes.name: Lemma 6.6: reduction to $r=1$
nodes.statement: In condition 2 of Proposition 6.4 it suffices to take $r = 1$, since after summing (13) over $r$ both sides are coalgebra morphisms $X(n) \otimes TV^{\otimes n} \to TV$, uniquely determined by their corestriction to cogenerators.
nodes.statement_clean: Reduces the structural identities to corestrictions onto cogenerators.
conclusions: Identity (15) for $r=1$ implies the identity for all $r$

nodes.name: Proposition 6.7: $P(X)$ is freely generated by $O(X)$
nodes.statement: The PROP $P(X)$ is freely generated as a PROP by the operad $O(X)$ formed by its $(n,1)$-ary operations; in general $O(X)$ need not be free.
nodes.statement_clean: Shows that $P(X)$ is generated as a PROP by an operad of single-output operations.
conclusions: $P(X)$ is freely generated by $O(X)$

nodes.name: Proposition 6.8: semi-freeness of $O(X)$
nodes.statement: If $X(n)$, $n \geq 1$, is semi-free as a dg operad with generating subspaces $V(n) \subset X(n)$, then both $P(X)$ and $O(X)$ are semi-free, freely generated by $\phi(v)^1_{k_1\ldots k_n}$ ($v \in V(n)$, $k_i \geq 1$, $n \geq 2$) and $D_k^1$, $k > 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Semi-freeness of $X$ is inherited by $P(X)$ and $O(X)$.
conclusions: $P(X)$ and $O(X)$ are semi-free as dg operads
Explicit free generators for $P(X)$ and $O(X)$

nodes.name: Proposition 6.9: $C\phi$ is a coalgebra morphism
nodes.statement: For a morphism $\phi: A \to \mathrm{Con}\, B$ of dg-coalgebras with counit (decomposed as $f, Tg, h$), the map $C\phi: \mathrm{Con}\, A \to \mathrm{Con}\, B$ defined by the matrix in (21) is a homomorphism of dg-coalgebras with counit.
nodes.statement_clean: The cone construction extends to morphisms.
assumptions: $\phi: A \to \mathrm{Con}\, B$ a coalgebra morphism with counit
conclusions: $C\phi: \mathrm{Con}\, A \to \mathrm{Con}\, B$ is a dg-coalgebra morphism with counit

nodes.name: Proposition 6.10: properties of operad $A$
nodes.statement: (1) $A$ is free as an operad of graded vector spaces, freely generated by the subspaces $V(n)$. (2) The counit map $\varepsilon: A \to As$ is a quasiisomorphism of operads of dg-coalgebras with counit.
nodes.statement_clean: $A$ is a free resolution of $As$ in operads of dg-coalgebras with counit.
conclusions: $A$ is free as operad of graded vector spaces with generators $V(n)$
$\varepsilon: A \to As$ is a quasiisomorphism

nodes.name: Proposition 6.11: free generation of $G$ and induced maps
nodes.statement: $G$ is freely generated by $\phi(v)^1_{k_1\ldots k_n}$ ($k_i \geq 1$) and $D_k^1$ ($k > 1$). The map $\varepsilon: A \to As$ produces $t': G \to B$ and $t: F \to B_\infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Specializes Propositions 6.8 and 6.10 to the operads $G$ and $F$.
conclusions: Explicit free generators of $G$
Maps $t': G \to B$ and $t: F \to B_\infty$ induced by $\varepsilon$

nodes.name: Proposition 6.12: surjectivity on cohomology
nodes.statement: The maps $r: F \to e_2$ and $r': G \to e_2\{-1\}$ induce surjections on cohomology, since it suffices to check this for $t'_*: H^\bullet(G(2)) \to H^\bullet(e_2\{-1\})$ and $G(2) \cong B(2)$ with $k: B(2) \to e_2\{-1\}(2)$ a quasiisomorphism by Theorem 4.2(1).
nodes.statement_clean: The maps to $e_2$ are cohomologically surjective; reducing the proof of quasi-isomorphism to upper bounds on cohomology.
conclusions: $r$ and $r'$ are surjective on cohomology

nodes.name: Lemma 6.13: $\phi_n$ modulo $F^2 P(A)$
nodes.statement: For $V$ a $P(A)$-algebra, $\phi_n(v, x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ is congruent modulo operations in $F^2 P(A)$ to the explicit expression (28) involving shuffles and the modified $\phi'_n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Computes $\phi_n$ up to second filtration step in terms of shuffles.
conclusions: Formula (28) holds modulo $F^2 P(A)$

nodes.name: Lemma 6.14: filtration $F'$ on $W$ is differential-compatible
nodes.statement: (1) The filtration $F'$ on $W = F^1 G/F^2 G$ generated by $\phi(v)^1_{n_1\ldots n_l}$ with $l \leq m$ and $D_l^1$ ($m \geq 1$) is compatible with the induced differential. (2) In $\mathrm{Gr}_{F'} W$, $d\phi(v)^1_{n_1\ldots n_l} = \phi(\delta v)^1_{n_1\ldots n_l}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The arity-filtration is differential-compatible and the induced differential matches $\delta$.
conclusions: $F'$ is compatible with $d$
Identification of $d$ with $\delta$ on the associated graded

nodes.name: Lemma 6.15: differential of $\phi_k$ modulo $F^3 G$
nodes.statement: $d\phi_k(x_1, \ldots, x_k) = \sum_{i=1}^{k} \phi_i\{T\phi_{k+1-i}\} + \sum_r (-1)^{r-1} \phi_{k-1}(x_1, \ldots, x_r \cup x_{r+1}, \ldots) + u$, where $u \in F^3 G$.
nodes.statement_clean: Closed form for $d\phi_k$ modulo three-step filtration.
conclusions: Explicit formula (34) for $d\phi_k$ mod $F^3 G$

nodes.name: Lemma 6.16: $Z \hookrightarrow W$ quasiisomorphism
nodes.statement: Let $Z \subset W$ be the $S$-submodule generated by images of $\phi(\mu_k)^1_{n_1\ldots n_k}$. Then (1) $Z$ is a subcomplex of $W$; (2) $\mathrm{Gr}_{F'} Z \to \mathrm{Gr}_{F'} W$ is a quasiisomorphism; (3) $Z \to W$ is a quasiisomorphism.
nodes.statement_clean: The fundamental-class-generated subcomplex captures the cohomology of $W$.
conclusions: $Z$ is a subcomplex
$Z \to W$ is a quasiisomorphism

nodes.name: Lemma 6.17: vanishing of higher $\phi_r(\mu_k)$
nodes.statement: The operations $\phi_r(\mu_k)(x_1, \ldots, x_k)$ for $k \geq 3$ and $\phi_r(\mu_2)(x_1 \otimes x_2) \mp \phi_r(\mu_2)(x_2 \otimes x_1)$ vanish whenever all $x_i \in T^1 V$ and $r \geq 2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Restricts the antisymmetrized operations to the subspace $V$, enabling the map $s'$.
conclusions: Vanishing of the listed operations for $r \geq 2$

nodes.name: Iso $\kappa: H^\bullet(B_\infty(2)) \cong e_2(2)$
nodes.statement: $\kappa: H^\bullet(B_\infty(2)) \xrightarrow{\;\cong\;} e_2(2)$, defined via the cohomology generators $\mu_{1,1}(x_1,x_2)+\mu_{1,1}(x_2,x_1)$ and $\tfrac{1}{2}(\mu_2(x_1,x_2)+\mu_2(x_2,x_1))$.

nodes.name: Map $\mathrm{Lie}\{1\} \to B_\infty$
nodes.statement: The operation $m_{1,1}(x_1,x_2) - m_{1,1}(x_2,x_1) \in B(2)$ satisfies the Jacobi identity and has zero differential, defining maps $\mathrm{Lie} \to B$ and $\mathrm{Lie}\{1\} \to B_\infty$.

nodes.name: Map $\phi: \mathrm{Holie}\{1\} \to HE_2$
nodes.statement: The forgetful map $\mathrm{Lie}\{1\} \to e_2$ (drop commutative product) lifts to a map of resolutions $\phi: \mathrm{Holie}\{1\} \to HE_2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.2(1) (sec. 5)
nodes.statement: Construct a functor from $e_2$-coalgebras to $B$-coalgebras using the Etingof-Kazhdan quantization, then exploit Proposition 5.1 to extract the unique map $B_\infty \to e_2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.2(2,3) (sec. 6)
nodes.statement: Build $F = O(A)\{1\}$ for the operad $A$ of chains on Stasheff associahedra, prove $r: F \to e_2$ is a quasiisomorphism via spectral sequences, and construct the map $s: \mathrm{Holie}\{1\} \to F$ using fundamental classes.

nodes.name: Proof that Theorem 4.1 implies Theorem 2.1 (sec. 4.1)
nodes.statement: Apply RLP to the cofibration $\phi: \mathrm{Holie}\{1\} \to HE_2$ (Lemma 4.1) in the closed model category of dg operads to lift across diagram (9), producing $\bar\phi: HE_2 \to F$ such that $q = r \circ \bar\phi$ satisfies Theorem 2.1.

nodes.name: Proof that Theorem 2.1 implies Kontsevich formality (sec. 2.2.3, 3)
nodes.statement: Use $q$ to upgrade $C^\bullet(A,A)$ to a homotopy $HE_2$-algebra; vanishing of obstructions (sec. 3) yields formality of $C^\bullet(A,A)$ and the Schouten/Gerstenhaber comparison via the diagram (7).

nodes.name: Set up obstruction bicomplex
nodes.statement: Identify coderivations of $P(V[1])$ with $\mathrm{Hom}_k(P(V[1]), V[1])$ and decompose the differential as $d_m + d_{br}$, giving a bicomplex $((\mathrm{Hom}_k(P(V[1]),V[1])^{gr_2,gr_3}, [d_m,\cdot], [d_{br},\cdot])$.

nodes.name: Compute $E_1$ via Harrison complex
nodes.statement: Use the iso $\mathrm{Hom}_k(S^k(T(V[1])/\mathrm{shuffles}[1])[-1], V[1]) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_{V^{\otimes k}}(S^k(\mathrm{Harr}(V[1]))[-1], V[1])$ to express the $d_m$-cohomology in terms of the Harrison complex.

nodes.name: Schouten case: $E_1^{0,k} = V[2] \otimes S^{1-k}(W[2]^*)$
nodes.statement: For $V$ the Schouten algebra ($V = S(W)$), $\mathrm{Harr}(V[1]) \simeq W[1] \otimes V[1]$, so $E_1^{0,k} \cong V[2] \otimes S^{1-k}(W[2]^*)$.

nodes.name: $E_2$ via de Rham differential
nodes.statement: Since $W = U \oplus U^*[-1]$ with $U = \mathbb{R}^n$, the differential $d_2$ induced by $d_{br}$ is the de Rham differential. Truncation of zeroth power kills all but $(0,0)$ cohomology, ruling out obstructions to formality.

nodes.name: Build dg Lie bialgebra $FreeLie\, V[1]$
nodes.statement: Given a dg $e_2$-coalgebra $V$, the free Lie algebra $FreeLie\, V[1]$ inherits a cocommutator $\bar\delta$ extending $\delta$ as a derivation, plus a bar-differential $b$, making it a dg Lie bialgebra.

nodes.name: Apply Etingof-Kazhdan quantization
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 5.1 to $FreeLie\, V[1]$ to obtain a dg-bialgebra structure on $U(FreeLie\, V[1])[[h]] \cong TV[1][[h]]$; track the auxiliary grading $|\cdot|$ and set $h = 1$ to obtain a topological dg-bialgebra on $\Pi TV[1]$.

nodes.name: Standardize the product via $\phi$
nodes.statement: Use the isomorphism $\phi(e_1 \otimes \ldots \otimes e_k) = e_1 * \ldots * e_k$ and its continuous inverse to conjugate $m, \Delta, d$ to the standard tensor-coalgebra structures, producing a $B_\infty$-algebra structure on $V$ and hence the desired functor and map $B_\infty \to e_2$.

nodes.name: Construct operad $A$ via Stasheff associahedra
nodes.statement: Define $A(n)_i = C_{-i}(K(n))$ where $K(n)$ are Stasheff associahedra equipped with an inductively built polyhedral decomposition and $0$-ary operations. Prop 6.10: $A$ is free as graded operad, and $\varepsilon: A \to As$ is a quasiisomorphism.

nodes.name: Filtration spectral sequence on $G$
nodes.statement: Equip $G$ with the filtration by number of internal vertices and analyze the $E_1$-page using the subcomplex $Z$ generated by $\phi(\mu_k)$. Identify $E_1^{\bullet,\bullet}$ as a free operad on $g = (e_2\{-1\})^*[-1]$, and show $d_1$ matches the differential of $HE_2\{-1\}$, hence $E_2 \cong e_2\{-1\}$ and $r': G \to e_2\{-1\}$ is a quasiisomorphism.

nodes.name: Construct $s: \mathrm{Holie}\{1\} \to F$
nodes.statement: Use the maps $\mathrm{Holie} \to \mathrm{Hoassoc} \to A$ ($m_k \mapsto (-1)^\sigma \mu_n$) and Lemma 6.17 to restrict the induced $\mathrm{Holie}$-algebra structure on $TV$ to $V$, yielding $s': \mathrm{Holie} \to G$ and $s: \mathrm{Holie}\{1\} \to F$ with the right behavior on $B_\infty$.

nodes.name: Spectral sequence analogy with Fulton-MacPherson compactifications
nodes.statement: The spectral sequence used in 6.4-6.5 for $F \to B_\infty \to e_2$ resembles that of the manifold-with-corners structure on Fulton-MacPherson compactifications of configuration spaces of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$; the author conjectures $F$ is a chain operad of configuration spaces for a suitable decomposition.

nodes.name: Heuristic origin of the proof
nodes.statement: The strategy was suggested by Boris Tsygan; the obstruction-vanishing approach echoes the homotopy Gerstenhaber structure on Hochschild cochains documented in Gerstenhaber-Voronov.
